entries.title: Cook–Levin: SAT is NP-complete
entries.summary: Every efficiently checkable bit-string problem reduces in polynomial time to satisfiability.
entries.scope: Explicit CNF encoding, total native-machine reductions, and UNSAT coNP-completeness.

entries.title: The PCP theorem
entries.summary: NP proofs can be checked with logarithmic randomness and constantly many nonadaptive queries.
entries.scope: Perfect completeness, soundness at most one half, and explicit native efficiency; construction constants are large.

entries.title: Fagin: logic captures NP
entries.summary: Existential second-order logic captures precisely the isomorphism-invariant NP properties of finite relational structures.
entries.scope: Finite relational signatures, explicit encodings, empty universes and nullary relations.

entries.title: Savitch: NPSPACE equals PSPACE
entries.summary: Nondeterminism does not enlarge polynomial space.
entries.scope: Native machines and polynomial space; this abstract states class equality rather than a parameterized quadratic-space bound.

entries.title: Reingold: undirected reachability is in L
entries.summary: Undirected graph connectivity can be decided with logarithmic work space.
entries.scope: Explicit unary-size header and adjacency-matrix encoding; native logspace, without a reduction-defined SL corollary.

entries.title: Immerman–Szelepcsényi: nondeterministic space is closed under complement
entries.summary: Nondeterministic space at least logarithmic is closed under complement; in particular NL equals coNL.
entries.scope: One finite-state native machine per problem, every-prefix work space c₁ s(n) + c₂ for any s with log₂ n ≤ s(n), no constructibility assumed, every branch terminating, arbitrary injective encodings; directed non-reachability on unary-header adjacency matrices as a corollary.

entries.title: Shamir: IP equals PSPACE
entries.summary: Interaction and randomness give a polynomial-time verifier the power of polynomial space.
entries.scope: All prover strategies are quantified explicitly, with a uniform native clock and specified completeness and soundness.

entries.title: Toda: a counting oracle decides the polynomial hierarchy
entries.summary: Every problem in the polynomial hierarchy is decidable in polynomial time with an exact counting oracle.
entries.scope: Witness counts and oracle bit answers are explicit; correctness holds for every extension of valid oracle answers.

entries.title: Barrington: five states capture NC¹
entries.summary: Polynomial-length permutation programs on five states capture logarithmic-depth polynomial-size Boolean circuits.
entries.scope: Nonuniform circuits and permutation programs; no uniform generator or compiler runtime is asserted.

entries.title: Håstad and Razborov–Smolensky: parity resists shallow circuits
entries.summary: At fixed depth, parity requires more than polynomially many gates, including over an odd-prime modular basis.
entries.scope: Explicit finite bounds, gate semantics and depth conventions; nonuniform lower bounds.

entries.title: Braverman: polylogarithmic independence fools AC⁰
entries.summary: Every k-wise independent distribution on n-bit strings with k ≥ (64q)^((2d+3)(d+7)+1) makes a circuit of NOT and unbounded fan-in AND/OR gates of depth at most d, with at most 2^q gates of fan-in below 2^q, output true with probability within 2^(-q) of the fraction of inputs on which it is true; for size and fan-in at most m and error ε this is k = (log(m/ε))^O(d²).
entries.scope: Arbitrary distributions with uniform marginals on every set of at most k positions; explicit bound with our own constants and exponent, weaker than Braverman's; size and depth count NOT gates and constants; one parameter q bounds the size, the fan-in and log₂ of the inverse error; nonuniform and information-theoretic.

entries.title: Formula lower bounds: parity and Andreev
entries.summary: Tree-shaped computation pays for repeated work: parity requires quadratic leaf size, and Andreev gives a stronger explicit bound.
entries.scope: De Morgan formulas, literal leaves, explicit block indexing and finite quantitative bounds; no general-circuit lower bound.

entries.title: Limaye–Srinivasan–Tavenas over any field (after Forbes): constant-depth algebraic circuits for IMM need superpolynomial size
entries.summary: Over every field, simple algebraic circuits (product gates reading distinct wires) of constant product-depth computing iterated matrix multiplication of d = ⌊log₂ ⌊log₂ n⌋⌋ generic n × n matrices need more than n^c gates for every c and all large n.
entries.scope: Any field, formal polynomials, unbounded fan-in sum and product gates, product gates reading distinct wires, size counting all gates; explicit non-asymptotic bound with exponent d^(1/(4^Δ-1)); constant product-depth Δ and the single value d = ⌊log₂ ⌊log₂ n⌋⌋; nonuniform.

entries.title: One-way functions yield pseudorandom generators and adaptive functions
entries.summary: One-wayness yields pseudorandomness, from an extra output bit to functions secure against adaptive oracle queries.
entries.scope: Uniform probabilistic polynomial time with explicit native evaluators, negligible advantage and full stateful oracle semantics; asymptotic security, not a concrete implementation audit.

entries.title: Gentry and GSW: fully homomorphic encryption from LWE
entries.summary: Bootstrapping the GSW scheme gives leveled fully homomorphic encryption from decision LWE, and fully homomorphic encryption under an additional circular-security assumption.
entries.scope: Explicit GSW key generation, encryption and decryption at a centered-binomial LWE family with quasi-polynomial modulus. The leveled scheme family E has joint native strict PPT runtime in (security, d) via NativeInDepth, its fresh-ciphertext key pair has the GSW key-generation law, and the fully homomorphic scheme's key generation is Gentry's self-loop key; the evaluator, the rest of the leveled keys and the decryption circuits are existential. Perfect correctness on fresh encryptions, fixed widths, uniformly generated polynomial-size decryption circuits, native strict PPT algorithms and asymptotic IND-CPA. Circular security is a separate hypothesis; no lattice hardness, circuit privacy, multi-hop evaluation or concrete loss.

entries.title: Haken: pigeonhole formulas require long resolution proofs
entries.summary: The pigeonhole principle has short CNF statements but requires exponentially many resolution lines.
entries.scope: The non-onto pigeonhole formula and a line-based resolution rule, with bound 2^(floor(n/24)); proof size is not solver runtime.

entries.title: Communication: disjointness and inner product resist randomness
entries.summary: Disjointness and parity of intersection require linear communication even with shared randomness and bounded error.
entries.scope: Binary protocol trees, worst-case cost and error at most one third on every input pair; explicit finite bounds and the final-answer convention.

entries.title: Sipser–Gács–Lautemann: BPP lies in the second polynomial level
entries.summary: Bounded-error randomized polynomial time admits both existential–universal and universal–existential polynomial descriptions.
entries.scope: Bit-string languages, fair independent random bits, correctness at least two thirds on every input, and total native polynomial-time tests; no derandomization assumption.

entries.title: Chor–Goldreich: the inner product extracts from two weak sources
entries.summary: Two independent weak random sources whose min-entropies add up to more than the string length give a nearly fair bit through the inner product modulo two.
entries.scope: Arbitrary sources with real min-entropy bounds, the exact bias bound 2^((n - k1 - k2)/2)/2 and its strong form, and sharpness at k1 + k2 = n; information-theoretic, with no running time asserted.

entries.title: OpenAI: the Exponential Time Hypothesis is false
entries.summary: For each fixed clause width, one deterministic native machine exactly counts satisfying assignments in subexponential time and polynomial space. Every fixed-width SAT exponent is zero, and ETH and SETH are false. Native formalization of OpenAI's manuscript, revised 25 October 2026, by the contributors to #1226.
entries.scope: Explicit CNF semantics, model counts over the occurring variables, and binary formula/output encodings; the interpolation-scale exponent n (log log (n + 16))² / sqrt(log(n + 16)) from §§3–6 and Proposition 6.4, where n is the number of variables, with polynomial time overhead and polynomial workspace in the encoded formula length. Includes all fixed widths and sizes; the count is exact on every formula of the given width. This does not establish the sharper Theorem 1.1 / Appendix D bound.

entries.title: Ilango: Partial MCSP is hard under the Exponential Time Hypothesis
entries.summary: Under the Exponential Time Hypothesis, deciding circuit size for partial Boolean functions requires at least quasi-polynomial time in the truth-table size. Note (October 2026): the native formalization of OpenAI's manuscript now proves ETH false; see the catalogue entry ‘OpenAI: the Exponential Time Hypothesis is false’. This conditional theorem is retained and remains valid, but its premise is false.
entries.scope: Explicit 3SAT and PartialMCSP encodings (both unary and binary size thresholds), De Morgan all-gates and binary-gate cost measures, and deterministic multi-tape subexponential-time lower bounds 2^o(m log m) = N^o(log log N).

entries.title: McKay–Murray–Williams: barely superlinear circuit lower bounds for MCSP separate P from NP
entries.summary: If NP has polynomial-size circuits, then MCSP on 2^n-bit truth tables has circuits of size 2^n poly(n + s(n)); hence barely superlinear MCSP lower bounds imply NP is not in P/poly and P ≠ NP.
entries.scope: Plain De Morgan circuits counting all operation gates, decision MCSP[n^k] on N = 2^n-bit truth tables in standard binary order, and native multi-tape P and NP; conditional magnification from a size lower bound at some arity per exponent.
